skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray showing complete opacification (white-out) of a hemithorax to determine the underlying etiology based on mediastinal position.
steps: Assess the direction of the mediastinal shift relative to the side of the opacity.
If the mediastinum is shifted contralaterally (away from the opacity), diagnose a space-occupying process such as a massive pleural effusion or large mass.
If the mediastinum is shifted ipsilaterally (toward the opacity), diagnose volume loss such as complete lung collapse/atelectasis.
If the mediastinum is central/midline, consider causes like pneumonia or combined effusion and collapse.

skills.trigger: When distinguishing between massive pleural effusion, lung collapse, and pneumothorax in the setting of unilateral thoracic pathology.
steps: Evaluate the density of the affected hemithorax: identify if it is opaque (white) or hyperlucent (dark).
Rule out pneumothorax if the hemithorax is opaque, as pneumothorax presents with hyperlucency and absent lung markings.
Differentiate opaque causes by checking mediastinal shift: contralateral shift indicates fluid/mass (effusion), while ipsilateral shift indicates collapse.
Select management based on this distinction (e.g., thoracentesis for effusion vs. bronchoscopy for collapse).
